implementation_notes: TypeScript inherits JavaScript's non-blocking model and adds typing that makes the channel's contract explicit - which is its real contribution. A bounded async queue is typed as Queue<T> with send (returns a Promise = backpressure by awaiting), receive (returns a Promise), and close (rejects or resolves every waiter with the terminal reason), so the 'never strand a waiter' rule is enforced by the interface rather than by convention. AbortSignal is the cancellation/close primitive. AsyncIterable/AsyncGenerator is the pull-based channel with natural backpressure, and for-await-of consumes it. For anything multi-worker or requiring strict FIFO fairness, a library (p-queue with concurrency control, or it-channel) is the right answer - a hand-rolled queue's lost-wakeup and fairness details are where TypeScript channels break, and the types do not catch that. The typing pattern that matters: model send as Promise<void> (not void) so the compiler forces the producer to await the backpressure.
idiom_name: typed bounded async queue (send: Promise<void> = backpressure, receive: Promise<T>, close) or AsyncGenerator for pull; AbortSignal for cancellation
pitfalls: send must return a Promise so the producer awaits the backpressure; a void send silently drops or blocks nothing.
close must reject or resolve EVERY waiting send/receive; a waiter left pending hangs the consumer forever - wire it to an AbortSignal.
A 'closed' channel that resolves receive() with undefined forever looks like 'no data yet' - distinguish closed from empty with a typed result ({value, done}) or an error.
An async generator that is not fully consumed (for-await breaks early) must have .return() called to run its finally, or the underlying resource leaks.
A hand-rolled async queue across workers loses wakeups and ordering; use a library (p-queue, it-channel) - types do not catch lost wakeups.
alternative: A library queue with concurrency control (p-queue, it-channel) for multi-worker or strict FIFO; a TaskGroup-equivalent (Promise.all with bounded concurrency) for fan-out/fan-in
